comments.author: Simon
comments.text:
FROM SIMON: Here are my suggestions:

1. It has been in my family since the day my parents got married.

('in my family' is a nicer phrase than 'kept' for this kind of sentence. Don't write 'the day OF my parents got married')

2. Whenever a friend comes to visit, I feel proud to explain the history of this sword.

3. Colour televisions were not available at that time.

4. We aren't really sure how long it has been in our family.

5. This item has been in my house for as long as I can remember.

(You can't say 'piece of item'. 'For a long time' is fine, but I decided to add some variety with the phrase 'for as long as I can remember')
